title: Take-Home Exercise 1 - Geospatial Analytics for Public Good
text:
In this take-home exercise, we are interested to investigate the spatial and spatio-temporal patterns of new businesses and firms established in Singapore for the first six months of 2025
The specific objectives of this take-home exercise are as follows:

To identify the “where” and “when” of new business entities, revealing clusters, patterns, and trends that are crucial for informed urban planning, resource allocation, and economic development.
To identify complex interaction patterns and emergent phenomena in the distribution of new businesses beyond simple proximity or density, such as clustering of related businesses, the influence of past trends on future locations, and the overall structural development of commercial areas, which are crucial for scientific urban planning and policy-making.

title: ISSS626 - GAA
text: Welcome! to the ISSS626 Geospatial Analytics & Application module. In this website, you will find the my coursework and Hands-on Exercise of this module of every week prepared for this course.

title: About
text:
about this site!
This website serves as a dedicated space for the submission of my academic work, including Hands-on Exercises and Take-home Exercises. It is designed to showcase my learning journey, practical applications of concepts, and problem-solving approaches. Each submission reflects the effort, knowledge, and skills I continue to build throughout my coursework.
The goal of this site is to provide a structured and organized way to track progress, document insights, and create a personal archive of completed exercises for future reference.

title: In-class_Ex04
text:
Preparing the Data
For this in-class exercise, Hunan shapefile and Hunan_2012 data file will be used.
Using the steps you learned from previous hands-on, complete the following tasks:

import Hunan shapefile and parse it into a sf polygon feature object.
import Hunan_2012.csv file parse it into a tibble data.frame.
join Hunan and Hunan_2012 data.frames.


Importing Hunan shapefile

hunan_sf <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                 layer = "Hunan")

Reading layer `Hunan' from data source 
  `K:\kalpitkulshrestha24\ISSS626\In-class Exercise\In-class Exercise 4\data\geospatial' 
  using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
Simple feature collection with 88 features and 7 fields
Geometry type: POLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 108.7831 ymin: 24.6342 xmax: 114.2544 ymax: 30.12812
Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84




Importing Hunan_2012 table

hunan2012 <- read_csv("data/aspatial/Hunan_2012.csv")



Joining Hunan and Hunan_2012

hunan_sf <- left_join(hunan_sf, hunan2012) %>%
  select(1:3, 7, 15, 16, 31, 32)

Mapping GDPPC

The codeDetermine adaptive bandwidthAICComputing geographically wieghted summary statisticsPreparing the output data



basemap <- tm_shape(hunan_sf) +
  tm_polygons() +
  tm_text("NAME_3", size=0.5)

gdppc <- qtm(hunan_sf, "GDPPC")
tmap_arrange(basemap, gdppc, asp=1, ncol=2)


Converting to SpatialPolygonDataFrame






Note



GWmodel presently is built around the older sp and not sf formats for handling spatial data in R.



hunan_sp <- hunan_sf %>%
  as_Spatial()
